title: Investigating marker accuracy in differentiating between university scripts written by students and those produced using ChatGPT
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether experienced markers can distinguish student-written coursework from text generated by ChatGPT-3.5. The authors frame the study as a response to concerns that generative AI may disrupt academic assessment, especially in writing-intensive higher education settings.

The study used a mixed-methods cross-sectional survey with 34 experienced academic and clinical academic markers from a medical school in Wales, UK. Participants reviewed undergraduate reflective writing scripts and postgraduate extended essays; in each set, two scripts were human-written and one was ChatGPT-generated. Markers graded scripts on writing style and content, then judged whether each script was written by a student, generated by ChatGPT, or uncertain. Open-ended responses were also collected and analyzed qualitatively.

Results showed low marker accuracy in identifying ChatGPT-authored work: only 23% correctly identified the undergraduate ChatGPT script and 19% correctly identified the postgraduate ChatGPT script. A significant effect of suspected authorship was found for script content but not writing style, suggesting content cues influenced judgments more than style. Qualitative findings indicated that language, structure, reflective depth, and referencing were the main cues used by markers. The authors conclude that even experienced markers struggle to reliably detect AI-generated writing, with referencing and some content features offering the strongest clues, but overall discrimination remained poor.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot / large language model system used to generate text responses from prompts and to assist with writing tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the comparator-generated text source (ChatGPT-3.5) for undergraduate reflective writing scripts and postgraduate extended essays; markers were asked to distinguish ChatGPT-generated scripts from student-written scripts.

findings.finding_summary: In this mixed-methods cross-sectional study with 34 experienced markers, only 23% correctly identified the ChatGPT-generated undergraduate reflective script and 19% correctly identified the ChatGPT-generated postgraduate essay. Markers were significantly affected by suspected author identity for content ratings, X(4, n=34)=10.41, p<0.05, but not for writing style.
findings.measure: Marker accuracy in identifying ChatGPT-authored scripts; grading of writing style and content

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical mixed-methods cross-sectional study, not an RCT or quasi-experiment, and it evaluates marker accuracy rather than learner outcomes. The evidence is informative but methodologically limited for causal claims.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational achievement effect size is reported, and the main outcomes are author-identification accuracy and content/style judgments. Findings suggest notable marker difficulty, but the practical impact on K-12 literacy instruction is indirect and unclear.
